topSpeedMPS.citation: J. Functional Morphology & Kinesiology, 2025, Post-PHV stage (~16.0yo): on-ice max speed (V0) 10.32+/-0.48 m/s (37 km/h). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12821503/

accel0to10mS.citation: Same source, Post-PHV 0-10m acceleration: 1.84+/-0.11s. (A second source, PMC11307188, gives 15.2-15.4yo elite/sub-elite 0-4m acceleration of 0.868s/0.914s -- not directly comparable to a 0-10m split, so not blended in here; kept as a cross-reference in docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md.)

avgAccelMPS2.citation: Computed from accel0to10mS via kinematics (d = 0.5*a*t^2, d=10m).

turningRadiusM.citation: No published turning-radius figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (0.6 * avgAccelMPS2).

stoppingDistanceM.citation: No published stopping-distance figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (2 * avgAccelMPS2).

reactionDelayS.citation: No ice-hockey-specific youth reaction-time study exists. This band is closest to the adult proxy data's own population (PMC11207928, mean age 25.2y is adult, but U18 is nearest to it of any band here); 250-350ms range applied flat across all bands per docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md.

passSpeedMPS.citation: Reference band for the pass-speed scaling used by every other profile: ~40mph, an engineering estimate deliberately kept well below the cited adult 70-110mph shot-velocity range (Anderson & Smith / Hache, https://ssl.wsu.edu/documents/2015/10/experimental-characterization-of-ice-hockey-sticks-and-pucks.pdf/), since a pass is gentler than a shot and U18 players are not yet at adult/pro strength. No direct youth pass-velocity study exists to calibrate against.

iceDecelerationMPS2.citation: mu*g using Hache's puck-on-ice friction coefficient (~0.1, https://physicsworld.com/a/physics-on-ice/) and standard gravity (9.81 m/s^2). Real, age-independent physical constant.
